content: World AIDS Day is observed annually on December 1 to increase awareness about the AIDS pandemic, which is caused by the spread of HIV infection. AIDS has resulted in the deaths of over 25 million individuals, and approximately 38.6 million people are currently living with HIV. This makes it one of the most devastating epidemics in human history. Despite advancements in access to antiretroviral therapy and medical care in many parts of the world, the epidemic still claimed an estimated 3.1 million lives in 2005 alone, including over 570,000 children. The idea for World AIDS Day was first proposed during the 1988 World Summit of Ministers of Health on Programmes for AIDS Prevention. Since its establishment, the day has been supported by governments, international organizations, and charitable groups worldwide. From its inception until 2004, the campaign for World AIDS Day was led by UNAIDS, which selected annual themes in collaboration with other global health organizations. In 2005, the responsibility for organizing the campaign was transferred to the World AIDS Campaign (WAC). The overarching theme chosen by WAC for World AIDS Day observances from 2005 to 2010 was Stop AIDS: Keep the Promise, with specific sub-themes selected each year. This theme is not limited to World AIDS Day but is also used throughout the year to promote HIV/AIDS awareness in the context of major global events, such as the G8 Summit. The World AIDS Campaign also conducts localized initiatives, such as the Student Stop AIDS Campaign in the United Kingdom, which focuses on educating young people about HIV infection and prevention. On World AIDS Day, it is common to hold memorial services to honor those who have died from HIV/AIDS. Government officials and public health leaders often participate in the day’s events by delivering speeches or hosting forums to discuss topics related to AIDS. Since 1995, the President of the United States has issued an official proclamation to mark World AIDS Day, and many other national governments have followed suit with similar announcements.
